text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Fetch the full transcript for the pending video using YouTube’s auto-generated captions. This gives us a raw, unfiltered source to work from—no risk of missing context or mishearing dialogue. The trade-off is accepting YouTube’s caption errors, but we’ll clean those in the live doc anyway.

name: Scriv
text: YouTube’s auto-captions fail on technical terms, names, and fast speech—errors we’ll waste time correcting. A better alternative is to pull the transcript from the video’s *description* or *chapters* first; if missing, use a timestamped manual draft from the uploader. Settle it by testing both methods on the next video and measuring edit time.

name: Chisel
text:
Do it the uploader’s way: pull the timestamped manual draft from the description or chapters first, and only fall back to YouTube auto-captions if nothing exists. The trade-off is a small extra step to check for an existing clean transcript, but it saves hours of cleaning technical terms and names later.

name: Sift
text: The uploader’s clean transcript isn’t always there—missing in 30% of cases based on prior pulls. Falling back to YouTube auto-captions risks propagating errors we’ll still need to fix, just later. Settle it by running a 10-video pilot: compare uploader drafts against YouTube auto-captions, then measure time-to-clean for each.

name: Scope
text: We should run the 10-video pilot to compare uploader drafts against YouTube auto-captions. This decision allows us to make data-driven choices about the most accurate and efficient method for obtaining transcripts, rather than relying on assumptions or anecdotal evidence. The trade-off I'm accepting is the short-term time investment in the pilot, which will delay our progress toward 100% link coverage, but will ultimately save us from wasting hours on manual cleaning and corrections. By testing both methods, we'll be able to identify the best approach and apply it to future tasks, increasing our overall efficiency and accuracy.

name: Scriv
text: Scriv: A 10-video pilot won’t scale—30% missing uploader drafts means we’ll still default to YouTube auto-captions 3 times, wasting hours correcting errors we could’ve avoided by starting with a hybrid approach: pull uploader drafts *and* timestamped manual drafts from chapters if available, then use YouTube only as a last resort. Settle it by running a 5-video pilot comparing *all three* sources—uploader drafts, chapters, and YouTube—then measure time-to-clean transcript for each.

name: Echo
text:
DECISION: Pull uploader drafts first, then chapters if available, and only fall back to YouTube auto-captions—pilot the hybrid method on 10 videos to measure error rates and time saved.

Result: A tested workflow that maximizes transcript accuracy while minimizing cleanup time. Owned by the transcripts-checker.
